data.narrative:
Deep Fission, a nuclear energy frontier-tech company founded by Liz and Rich Muller, is preparing for IPO after raising $80M in prior rounds. The valuation universe consists of 9 peers across nuclear energy: 3 public companies (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 6 private firms including Helion, Oklo, Valar Atomics, X-Energy, and Nano Nuclear Energy.

Peer-median valuation analysis was not applicable. The nuclear energy sector contains only 6 same-sector peers total, but none satisfy narrow filtering criteria (same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar valuation tier)—each filter yielded fewer than 3 datapoints, the minimum threshold for reliable median estimation. Applying an all-sector median would introduce material distortion given the heterogeneity in capital requirements, commercialization timelines, and technology maturity across nuclear subsegments.

Without sufficient narrow-peer triangulation, this analysis cannot support a specific valuation range. The path forward requires either: (1) expansion of the comp set using adjacent frontier-energy peers with analogous capital and regulatory intensity; (2) expansion of nuclear peers through secondary research into later-stage or recently acquired private companies; or (3) application of DCF-based methods using Deep Fission's specific unit economics and regulatory timeline. The scarcity of IPO-stage nuclear comparables reflects market structure rather than data limitation.
